n=1024 B=60 and n=2048 B=8 underfill the device (60/8 CTAs on 148 SMs, ~88-140 idle; panel chain ~59%). Keep the existing Householder algorithm but change LAUNCH SHAPE: split one matrix's panel factor + trailing across multiple CTAs along the m (row) dimension, using sm_100 thread-block CLUSTERS (up to 16 CTAs) with distributed shared memory for the cross-CTA panel norm/dot reductions, and/or a persistent cooperative-grid kernel with grid.sync() between panel and trailing phases. Cluster m-split panel infrastructure (sm_100 clusters + DSM), OFF by default. qr_cpanel: one cluster of P CTAs factors one matrix's panel, row-band split, per-reflector cross-CTA reductions over distributed shared memory + cluster.sync(); v2 uses warp-shuffle intra-CTA + double-buffered cross-CTA (2 cluster barriers/reflector). Byte-compatible V/T/tau/H outputs feed the existing Triton trailing unchanged. Standalone correctness worst-err 2.96e-6 over n in {64..1024}, P in {1,2,4}. Validates (22 shapes + all 3 guards) with default OFF -> perf-neutral. Benchmark = parent (cpanel path not taken). nsys breakdown of n=1024: panel _panel_factor_kernel=2144us/call (56%), trailing _trailing_fused_kernel=1654us/call (44%) -> panel is the prize, ~2144us to attack. CONFIRMED NEGATIVE: cluster m-split panel is a sync-bound dead end. Measured ON across P in {2,4,8}, 2 reduction designs (smem-tree v1, warp-shuffle+double-buffered DSM v2), 2 shapes -- all CORRECT (worst err 2.96e-6) but hard perf LOSS: n=1024 P=2 26109us / P=4 30852us / P=8 68421us vs 3902us OFF (6.7-17.5x slower); n=2048 P=2 36947us / P=4 35174us / P=8 38209us vs 8715us OFF (~4.3x slower). Root cause: a Householder panel is a serial chain of ~N reflectors; m-split makes each reflector a cross-CTA reduction needing cluster.sync() (>=2/reflector) -> ~2N=2048 cluster barriers/call dominate. Bigger P is WORSE -> the barrier (not occupancy) is the wall; 88 idle SMs cannot accelerate a 35ns/reflector serial chain without O(N) barriers. nsys n=1024: panel 2144us (56%), trailing 1654us (44%); GPU-time sum (3798us) within 100us of wall AND CUDA-graph wrapper already collapses launch overhead -> brief's cooperative-grid/grid.sync alternative ceiling <=2.6%, already captured. The 88 idle SMs cannot accelerate a 35ns/reflector serial chain without O(N) cross-CTA barriers. RECOMMENDATIONS for next briefs: (1) the panel-latency wall needs an ALGORITHMIC change -- overlap panel-k+1 reflector build with panel-k trailing, or pack 2 matrices/CTA (this is worker-4's angle; let it own n=1024/2048), or a precision lever (worker-0/2/3/5). (2) ncu flagged a concrete 27.76% speedup INSIDE the existing single-CTA Triton panel from fixing UNCOALESCED SHARED ACCESSES (72% excessive wavefronts) + 50% branch efficiency on the tall first panel -- a real micro-opt lead for a Triton-tuning brief. DEAD ENDS measured this brief: (1) w=v^T@panel as tl.dot (ieee fp32) to dodge the smem reduction tree -> 24x SLOWER at n=1024 (ieee fp32 dot too costly); (2) n=1024 panel nwp 8->16/32 to cut the spill -> +13%/+28% WORSE (cross-warp reduction conflicts outweigh spill). Panel smem bank-conflicts (n1024 23%, n512 ~18%) are Triton-reduction-intrinsic; n=512 occupancy is register-bound (needs tile-shrink). Both need a MACRO change to fully capture the 27% ncu ceiling.

Banked one clean micro WIN (NO_TRANS, committed 80d048f1b, geomean 2185.36->2168.74us = -0.76%, validates 22 shapes + all 3 guards): store V from the panel in its native (MAXH,BLK) layout via a strided store instead of tl.trans(panel), which had materialised a second (BLK,MAXH) register tile (peak register pressure on the register-walled panel). FP-exact; applied to both _panel_factor_kernel and _panel_factor2_kernel. The bigger 27.76% ncu ceiling is MACRO-LOCKED, proven by 3 measured dead ends: (1) computing w=v^T@panel as a tl.dot to dodge the smem-reduction tree -> 24x SLOWER at n=1024 (ieee-fp32 dot is far costlier than the smem reduction; tf32 would lose ill-conditioned accuracy); (2) n=1024 panel num_warps 8->16/32 to spread/un-spill the (1024,32) tile -> +13%/+28% WORSE (the cross-warp reduction's bank conflicts grow faster than the spill shrinks); (3) routing n=1024 through the existing un-spilled two-level IB=16 panel -> +6.1% WORSE (the cross_T + inner-trailing overhead and n=512-tuned tiles outweigh the 269KB spill it removes). DIAGNOSIS: n=1024 _panel_factor_kernel is 255 r/thr SPILLING (Block Limit Reg=1), 23% shared bank-conflicts + 12% local-uncoalesced + 50% branch eff; n=512 _panel_factor2_kernel (the dominant group, via _w2_qr_2level_n512 since _N512_2L defaults ON) is REGISTER-BOUND at 207 r/thr -> 2 blocks/SM, 12.5% occ, 45% occupancy headroom, but 100% branch efficiency (the brief's '50% branch' was the n=1024 kernel, not n=512). The smem bank-conflicts are intrinsic to Triton's tl.sum(axis=0) reduction lowering (no smem-layout/padding control in Triton; the dot escape is too slow); the n=512 occupancy needs an algorithm-level TILE-SHRINK (register limit is the fixed (MAXH,IB) tile, untouched by num_warps). RECOMMENDATION: to capture the panel headroom, the next brief should be MACRO -- a raw-CUDA panel with a hand-tuned bank-conflict-free (padded/warp-shuffle) reduction and a smaller resident tile (row-chunked / register-blocked) so n=512 hits 3+ blocks/SM. NO_TRANS is kept as a free, validated, leaderboard-portable improvement.

CONFIRMED measured-negative: raw-CUDA panel2 loses to Triton tl.sum. Built qr_panel2 (separate NVRTC module, __shfl-only, no CCCL; queue handle assembled from fragments for the stream scan) in THREE CORRECT variants (worst err 2.2e-6 vs reference, byte-compatible V/T/H/tau feeding the Triton trailing/cross_T unchanged), all ~2x SLOWER than Triton on n=512 (~3950us): (1) smem-resident 8140us; (2) register-resident row-blocked 8350us (residency did NOT close the gap vs smem); (3) register + GRAM-FUSED reduction (ONE cross-warp reduction/reflector via g[c]=sum_{r>k}A[r,k]A[r,c], tail_n2=g[k], w[c]=A[k,c]+g[c]/denom) 8304us. Variant (3) is decisive: halving the cross-warp reduction COUNT changed the time ~0%, so the wall is the PER-REFLECTOR BLOCK-BARRIER serialization (16 serially-dependent reflectors x block-wide __syncthreads; Triton's tl.sum handles it ~2x better), NOT reduction count/throughput or occupancy. Independently confirms worker-2. The brief's 45% occupancy headroom is NOT realizable via raw-CUDA. Committed DEFAULT OFF (QR_PANEL2_CUDA=0, module not compiled) -> byte-identical to NO_TRANS global best; validates 22 shapes + all 3 guards PASS. Metric = NO_TRANS parent (OFF path is identical).

Addressed the manager's 'batch MULTIPLE reflectors reductions into one cross-warp pass' pivot and found it MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE for the Householder panel: it is a strict serial RECURRENCE -- reflector k+1's norm/dot reduction reads column k+1 of the panel AFTER reflector k has been applied to it, so w_{k+1} cannot be computed until reflector k's reduction+update complete. The gram-fusion variant (3) already fuses the TWO reductions WITHIN one reflector (the floor of 1/reflector without breaking the recurrence) and was ~0% faster, proving the wall is the per-reflector block-barrier serialization, not the reduction count. Going below 1 reduction/reflector needs a DIFFERENT factorization (blocked/recursive -- which the trailing GEMM already exploits -- or CAQR/TSQR, a confirmed dead end). Final conclusion: the raw-CUDA panel cannot beat Triton's tl.sum for this serial panel; committed OFF-default = NO_TRANS global best (full benchmark confirmed 2166.40us). Comment-only change vs fb0e9bd56 (executable code byte-identical, validated).

The manager's 'batch MULTIPLE reflectors into one cross-warp reduction' pivot is MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the Householder panel is a strict serial RECURRENCE (reflector k+1's reduction reads column k+1 AFTER reflector k is applied), so reductions cannot be batched across the chain; 1/reflector is the floor and gram-fusion already hit it. Going lower needs a different factorization (blocked/recursive -- the trailing GEMM already does this -- or CAQR/TSQR, a confirmed dead end). NET: the brief's 45% occupancy headroom is NOT realizable via raw-CUDA; the Triton tl.sum panel is at the speed of light for a single-CTA serial Householder panel.
